title: Review
description: Response body of GET /api/reviews/{id}, POST /api/reviews, POST /api/reviews/upload, POST /api/reviews/{id}/rerun, and each item of GET /api/reviews.

status.description: 'completed' means the engine finished, never that a human approved it.

report_status.description: The engine's own report status, once a report has been received.

error_summary.description: Safe message only; never a raw provider error or stack trace.

served_from_cache.description: True when the findings were replayed from the per-account result cache.

required_reviewer_role.description: Always null on new reviews (individual-user mode: routing is off). Older rows may hold a role name; it no longer restricts approval.

text.description: The content version's text; finding spans are code-point offsets into it.

rules_status.description: Brand rules on this review. complete: every check ran; incomplete: a check failed (never show the draft as rule-clean); not_applied: nothing ran (see error_summary). Null on reviews from before rules existed.

rule_checks.description: One record per rule. not_checkable means 'not checked' (the draft lacks what the check needs), never 'passed'.

locked_phrases.description: Intent-lock: the reviewed version's must-keep phrases (exact, case-sensitive). No suggestion that removes one is offered.

allowed_actions.description: Round 3: what the signed-in user may do with this review, computed by the server with the same rule its routes enforce (docs/governance.md 9.2). Values: create_version, rerun, approve, request_changes, reject, comment, dismiss_finding; Phases 3-4 add submit, resubmit, assign, mark_reviewed, publish. Show a control only when its action is listed; treat unknown values as unknown.

is_current_version.description: Round 3: true when this review's content version is the draft's current one. null on idempotency replays recorded before this field existed.

approval_mode.description: Round 3: "self" when nobody but the draft's author could approve it, so the author's own sign-off is allowed and recorded as a self-approval (decision D1); "team" otherwise, where the author can never approve. null on replays recorded before this field existed.
